paper.title_en: Finite-distance weak-field lensing for spacetimes without photon spheres
paper.abstract_en: We apply the reference-renormalized curvature primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism to finite-distance weak gravitational lensing in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes where photon sphere normalization is unavailable, unnecessary, or not the most natural primitive gauge choice. In this approach, the additive freedom of the radial curvature primitive is fixed by matching to an appropriate reference optical geometry rather than by imposing a vanishing condition at a circular null orbit. This makes the method directly applicable to geometries with no accessible photon sphere while preserving compatibility with orbit-normalized prescriptions whenever such orbits exist. We first formulate a practical photon sphere diagnostic based on the monotonicity of $C(r)/A(r)$ and a corresponding algorithm for constructing the reference-normalized primitive. We then apply the method to the super-extremal Reissner-Nordström naked singularity in the no-photon sphere sector $Q^2>9\,M^2/8$, emphasizing the distinction between the exact reference-normalized primitive and the weak-deflection expression obtained by evaluating that primitive on a reference ray. Additional applications include the Joshi-Dey-Joshi-Bambhaniya naked singularity, JMN-1 and JMN-2 collapse-generated naked singularities, the massless Barriola-Vilenkin global monopole, and the negative-mass Schwarzschild geometry. The examples show that the absence of a photon sphere obstructs only one possible primitive gauge choice, not the finite-distance Gauss-Bonnet lensing construction itself. Reference normalization provides a uniform calculational framework for black-hole metrics, naked singularity geometries, matched interiors, and conical backgrounds, provided the optical domain is Riemannian and the weak-deflection configuration is single-pass.
